Description:
The NURBS twin of EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam: two cylinders of the SAME radius whose axes cross at a
right angle, so that the two mantles TOUCH TANGENTIALLY at two points and the intersection curve has a
node at each of them. What is new here is that neither surface is a CylindricalSurface. Both bodies are
solid.extrude of an exact nine pole rational NURBS circle, so both mantles are SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion
and nothing about them is known in closed form - the contact has to be FOUND, not derived.

  cylZ   r = 10 about the z axis, z from -20 to 30
  cylY   r = 10 about the y axis, y from -20 to 25

Because the radii are equal, the intersection of the two infinite mantles degenerates into TWO ELLIPSES
lying in the planes z = y and z = -y, and those two ellipses cross at

  (10, 0, 0)  and  (-10, 0, 0)

At each of them both surfaces have the same tangent plane x = +-10 and the intersection curve has a NODE
- two branches crossing in one point. This is the degeneracy the case is about, and on these surfaces it
is exactly the one Surfaces.TangentialContacts has to reach through its general search on ISurface: the
canal form is only available for the natural quadrics, and a SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion is none.

The nodes are placed on the WORST possible spot of the topology, as in the quadric case. The nine pole
circle starts at its first pole, so cylZ's seam is the line x = 10, y = 0 and cylY's seam is the line
x = 10, z = 0 - both run straight through the node at (10, 0, 0). The second node at (-10, 0, 0) sits on
the fifth pole of both circles, which is a knot of the NURBS and therefore a span boundary but not a
seam. So the case carries both flavours at once: a node on a face boundary and a node in the interior of
a face but on a patch boundary.

The lengths are of different and asymmetric extent for the reason EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam gives:
with symmetric cylinders the halves a difference falls into are congruent, the canonical order of the
parts of a multi solid result is then not determined, and the recorded extents flip from run to run.
Expected:
Every value in this case is exact - it is the same geometry as EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam, only built
out of NURBS, so the two baselines can be read against each other field by field. Any difference in
volume, area or extent between the two cases is a defect in one of them; a difference in the number of
faces is not, because the two constructions partition the mantles differently.

  cylZ   V = pi*100*50 = 15707.9632679490, A = 2*pi*10*50 + 2*pi*100 = 3769.9111843078,
         extent -10, -10, -20 .. 10, 10, 30
  cylY   V = pi*100*45 = 14137.1669411541, A = 3455.7519189488,
         extent -10, -20, -10 .. 10, 25, 10

The intersection is the STEINMETZ SOLID of two equal cylinders, whose volume and area are known exactly:
  crossInter   V = 16*r^3/3 = 5333.3333333333
               A = 16*r^2   = 1600.0000000000  (no cap is reached, the body stays inside |y|,|z| <= 10)
               extent -10, -10, -10 .. 10, 10, 10
It is a single solid bounded by cylindrical faces meeting at the two nodes, with no planar face.

From that everything else follows exactly:
  crossUnion     15707.9632679490 + 14137.1669411541 - 5333.3333333333 = 24511.7968757698
  crossZminusY   15707.9632679490 - 5333.3333333333 = 10374.6299346157
  crossYminusZ   14137.1669411541 - 5333.3333333333 =  8803.8336078208

The SHAPE of the differences is the interesting part, and it is where a mishandled node shows up first.
In the plane z = 0 the cross section of cylZ is the full disc of radius 10 and cylY removes all of it,
so crossZminusY falls apart into a lower and an upper half connected ONLY through the two node points
(10, 0, 0) and (-10, 0, 0):
  pi*100*20 - 5333.3333333333/2 = 3616.5186405129  and  pi*100*30 - 2666.6666666667 = 6758.1112941027
and likewise crossYminusZ, split in the plane y = 0 into
  3616.5186405129  and  pi*100*25 - 2666.6666666667 = 5187.3149673078
What must NOT happen is that a half is dropped, that two halves are welded into a manifold body, or that
the operation returns nothing at all.

WHY THESE RADII AND NOT OTHERS - HISTORICAL, THE DEFECT IS FIXED. A planar face whose outline is a
rational NURBS circle used to be measured through Border.Area -> BSpline2D.GetArea ->
GeneralCurve2D.GetArea -> Approximate(false, 0.0), and for most radii that biarc approximation
degenerated into four straight lines, so the lid measured 2*r*r instead of pi*r*r. It was not even a
threshold: exact for r = 9.5, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 18, 19 and short by the factor 2/pi for r = 2.5, 4, 5,
6, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 20, 22, 25. Every radius in this case was therefore taken from the first list, so
that its numbers would be the geometry and not a measurement artefact.
Since 2026-09-21 BSpline2D integrates the swept area of a rational spline instead of approximating it
(Gauss-Legendre with panel doubling), and every radius is exact. The radii here are left as they are -
they cost nothing and the case does not need rewriting - but a new case no longer has to avoid any.
Status:
OK since 2026-09-18. The case was a KNOWN FAILURE from 2026-09-17 until RefineCurveIntersection was added
to ISurfaceImpl.Intersect (c98950cc): before that crossUnion returned the two operands unchanged and both
differences died in a Debug.Fail inside the boolean operation. All four operations now produce the right
SHAPE, which is what this case is about:

  crossInter    ONE solid, four SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion faces meeting in the two nodes at (+-10, 0, 0),
                no planar face - the Steinmetz solid, in substance identical to the crossInter of the
                quadric twin EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam
  crossUnion    ONE solid, 12 faces, closed and consistent
  crossZminusY  TWO solids, joined only through the two node points, as the Expected section demands
  crossYminusZ  TWO solids, likewise
No half is dropped, nothing is welded into a manifold body and no operation returns nothing - the three
failure modes the Expected section names.

HOW CLOSE THE NUMBERS ARE, against the exact values of the Expected section:
  crossInter    volume 5333.32016311  against 5333.3333333333            2.5e-06
                area   1600.01431688  against 1600                       8.9e-06
  crossUnion    volume 24515.9686461  against 24511.7968757698           1.7e-04
  crossZminusY  6758.74444589 + 3617.09670395 against
                6758.1112941027 + 3616.5186405129                        1.2e-04 on the sum
  crossYminusZ  5187.94549362 + 3617.12135006 against
                5187.3149673078 + 3616.5186405129                        1.4e-04 on the sum
The operands themselves are good to 2.5e-09, so the ~1e-04 of the three boolean results is the error of
the tangential construction and not of the input. The exact identity union + intersect = cylZ + cylY
misses by 4.16 of 29845.13, again 1.4e-04, and in the same direction: the union overshoots. Note that
crossInter, which was already right before the fix, is two orders of magnitude better than the three
results that the fix unlocked - there is still something to gain here.

THE ONE THING THAT GOT WORSE, and it is the next thing to look at in this case. crossInter reaches y and
z only to +-9.94946412 where the Steinmetz solid reaches exactly +-10, an absolute miss of 0.0505. The
recorded extent used to be +-10.000000001. The two ellipses are marched, and their branches stop short of
the extreme point - the debug trace of the run shows branch heads at 9.9484 - so the point where the
intersection curve reaches y = z = 10 is never hit. Volume and area barely show it because the missing
sliver is second order; the extent shows it directly. Whether the extreme position is not searched for or
the marching gives up before it is open.

Compare NurbsCylindersCrossedDifferentRadii: the identical construction with radii 10 and 12 instead of
10 and 10, so with no contact at all, is green. The difference between the two cases is the tangency and
nothing else.

Four faces meeting in two vertices - the two nodes at (+-10, 0, 0) - and no planar face, as in the quadric twin EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam. The extent is the weak spot and the open defect of this case: y and z reach only +-9.94946412 instead of +-10, see Status.
